name: Etched Note
summary: At Camp Narache, Etched Note calls a young tauren hunter to train with Lanka Farshot. The message begins their study of the wild.

sections.title: A Summons to the Hunt
sections.body: Grull Hawkwind gives the etched message to a young tauren skilled in marksmanship and tracking. The novice has trained among the bluffs of Red Cloud Mesa. Lanka Farshot has noticed the youth's bloodline and raw ability, and calls them to study under his watch.

sections.title: Tradition of the Plains
sections.body: Among the Shu'halo, hunters scout and fight, but they serve the tribes in other ways too. They provide food with their quarry, guard nomadic camps, and keep close to Kalimdor's beasts. Lanka begins with weapons and Mulgore's creatures. In time, the novice may learn the ancient art of taming wild companions.

faq.q: What is the purpose of the Etched Note?
aliases: why did i get etched note
faq.answer: Etched Note calls a novice tauren hunter to train with Lanka Farshot at Camp Narache.
Grull Hawkwind passes along the note. He says a messenger from the hunter trainer sought out the young hunter moments earlier.
Lanka Farshot is in Camp Narache on Red Cloud Mesa, near the hunter training grounds, ready to instruct new hunters.

faq.q: Why are hunters so revered among the tauren?
faq.answer: Hunters feed the tauren, read the wilderness, and keep harmony with the spirits of the plains.

faq.q: What skills does this training introduce?
faq.answer: Lanka teaches basic hunting, ranged weapons, and knowledge of wild beasts. In time, he may teach the rites for taming animal companions.

faq.q: What is the next step after reading the note?
faq.answer: You can report to Lanka Farshot in Camp Narache to begin training. He teaches you to fire your rifle, tame a pet, and more as you grow.

angles.text: As a hunter, you begin learning marksmanship, survival in the wild, and life with beast companions.
As Shu'halo, you honor the Earth Mother by respecting the beasts that sustain your tribe across Mulgore's plains.
